title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix
book_title: Prologue: The Business, The Price & Our Independent Verdict

epigraph.quote: A surging order book can make a stock look unstoppable on the way up, but only free cash flow, clean footnotes, and balance-sheet discipline protect you when the tape shifts into Stage 3.
epigraph.author: Independent Underwriting Prologue

web_blocks.html: Marine Electricals (India) Ltd. (NSE: MARINE) serves two fast-growing Indian capex cycles: naval warships and hyperscale data centers [2, 11]. Its open order book surged sevenfold to ₹3,514 Cr by September 30, 2026 (4.01x FY26 sales of ₹877 Cr) [7]. On November 16, 2026, management won two more orders worth ₹233.21 Cr (excl. taxes) from STT Global Data Centres India and Ganges Shipyard [28]. That lifts pro-forma backlog toward ₹3,747 Cr before Q3 billing. Q2 FY27 sales jumped 82.07% YoY to ₹404.65 Cr, with 12% OPM and 92.75% YoY PAT growth to ₹31.79 Cr [7, 23].

Our refreshed audit keeps business quality at CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL (PASS_WITH_WATCH). Pass 1 uncovered three material blind spots in Chapters 1–6. First, ICRA warns most contracts are fixed-price, and Data Centre margins are not broken out in audited accounts [30]. Second, footnotes hold ₹31.36 Cr in GE arbitration exposure, a ₹14.88 Cr GST demand, and consolidated audit exceptions [31, 32]. Third, promoters bought 70% of MEL Shipyard for ₹70,000 in June 2026, while the parent backs loss-making Evigo Charge with a ₹25 Cr guarantee [33, 34]. At the 2026-11-25 live TradingView close of ₹400.60 (2026-11-23 NSE close ₹406.95), MARINE trades at 70.44x TV P/E (69.8x Screener) in STAGE_3. New Capital is REJECTED (TIER_0) on Valuation, Cash Flow, and Trend. The 125-share (1.19%) Zerodha holding stays HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP with the stop ratcheted UP from ₹313.40 to ₹327.13.

web_blocks.html: This refresh shows why blind-first underwriting matters when order headlines look dazzling. Marine Electricals grew from a ₹236 Cr FY15 marine shop into a ₹1,152 Cr TTM electrical supplier [1]. Its ₹3,514 Cr backlog plus ₹233.21 Cr in November 16 orders give real revenue visibility [7, 28]. The 160,000 sq. ft. Goa PTU plant and 59.20% subsidiary Marks Marine Radio anchor its niche in data centers and naval ships [9, 30].

Yet the cash-flow and governance hurdles have grown sharper. Over FY17–FY26, cumulative operating cash flow (₹93 Cr) covered only 44.5% of net profit (₹209 Cr) [1]. Ten-year cumulative free cash flow is -₹48 Cr (-₹43 Cr in FY26). Debtor Days stand at 178, and Other Assets reached ₹953 Cr (87% of total assets) [1]. Add fixed-price margin risk, ₹31.36 Cr in GE arbitration exposure, a ₹14.88 Cr GST demand, and the ₹70,000 MEL Shipyard sale to promoters [30, 31, 32, 33]. At 70.44x P/E in Stage 3, fresh capital has no margin of safety [34].

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our refreshed, independent institutional dossier on Marine Electricals (India) Limited. Over the next nine chapters, we apply a strict two-pass discipline: first stripping away the stock price, prior targets, and prior verdicts to re-test our baseline assumptions and hunt for forensic blind spots across Chapters 1 through 6; and second, unlocking the live November 25, 2026 TradingView tape alongside our November 23, 2026 NSE portfolio ledger in Chapters 7 through 9.

On the surface, Marine Electricals' momentum looks electric. On top of a ₹3,514 Cr September 30, 2026 order book — four times FY26 revenue — management disclosed ₹233.21 Cr in fresh November 16 orders from STT Global Data Centres India and Ganges Shipyard, taking pro-forma visibility toward ₹3,747 Cr. Quarterly revenue jumped 82% year-on-year in Q2 FY27, and net profit nearly doubled.

Yet our blind-spot audit uncovered three critical risks that did not sit in the baseline narrative: ICRA's warning that most contracts are fixed-price without audited Data Centre segment margin breakouts; ₹31.36 Cr in GE Power Conversion solar EPC arbitration exposure plus a ₹14.88 Cr GST demand and consolidated audit exceptions; and related-party governance flags including the June 2026 transfer of 70% of MEL Shipyard directly to promoters for ₹70,000 alongside a ₹25 Cr guarantee on loss-making Evigo Charge. Layered onto 44.5% ten-year CFO-to-PAT conversion, negative ₹48 Cr ten-year free cash flow, and 178 debtor days, the picture demands discipline.

At the live November 25, 2026 TradingView close of ₹400.60 (November 23 NSE ledger close ₹406.95), MARINE trades at 70.44x trailing earnings and has slipped into Stage 3 below both its 10-week EMA and 50-day SMA. Our independent verdict is clear: REJECTED (TIER_0) for new capital, while our 125-share (1.19% weight) Zerodha position stays HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP with the structural stop ratcheted UP from ₹313.40 to ₹327.13.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: WHY WE REFRESHED THIS DOSSIER BLIND
book_callouts.text: If you only read press releases, a ₹233.21 Cr STT Data Centre order win looks like an automatic buy-the-dip signal. By stripping the chart away first and auditing ICRA rationales, litigation footnotes, and related-party transfers, we avoid paying 70x earnings for hidden risks.

book_subsections.title: What Changed Since November 13: New Orders, New Forensics & Stage 3 Tape
paragraphs: Four concrete developments separate this November 25 refresh from our November 13 baseline. First, on the commercial side, Marine Electricals won ₹233.21 Cr in fresh orders on November 16 from STT Global Data Centres India and Ganges Shipyard, filed an updated November 23 Investor Presentation, and converted Marks Marine Radio into a 59.20% consolidated subsidiary.

Second, our Pass 1 blind-spot audit patched Chapters 1, 2, 3, 5, and 6 with material forensic realities: fixed-price contract inflation exposure, bundled Industry segment reporting, ₹31.36 Cr GE arbitration exposure, ₹14.88 Cr GST demand, Eltech going-concern and audit-trail exceptions, the ₹70,000 promoter buyout of 70% of MEL Shipyard, and ₹25 Cr in parent guarantees backing loss-making Evigo Charge.

Third, the technical tape shifted from Stage 2 into Stage 3 (WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT_RETEST): MARINE dropped from ₹426.85 to ₹406.95 on the November 23 NSE ledger and ₹400.60 on the November 25 live TradingView snapshot, slipping below both its 10-week EMA (₹404.40) and 50-day SMA (₹422.22). Fourth, our Zerodha holding increased from 25 shares to 125 shares (₹51,604.15 cost basis, 1.19% portfolio weight), making our upward-only stop-loss ratchet from ₹313.40 to ₹327.13 essential.

book_subsections.title: How to Navigate This Ten-Chapter Monograph
paragraphs: Every figure in this monograph is anchored to audited ten-year filings, NSE Regulation 30 disclosures, ICRA credit rationales, and two explicitly separated market timestamps: the November 23, 2026 NSE ledger cutoff (₹406.95 close; ₹42.64 lakh IN portfolio net worth) and the live November 25, 2026 TradingView snapshot (₹400.60 close; 70.44x TV P/E).

Chapters 1 through 6 keep the stock price locked out so you can judge the naval moat, Goa PTU economics, fixed-price margin risks, subsidiary governance, and 44.5% ten-year cash conversion objectively. Chapters 7 through 9 then open the live market screen to show why new capital is REJECTED (TIER_0) while existing Zerodha shares are managed mechanically via our ₹327.13 ratcheted stop and ₹465.62 exit-into-strength alert.
